left.title: What to watch for in the battle for the Senate
left.body: Apart from who wins the White House, which party wins the Senate majority is probably the biggest open question of 2020. To have a governing majority next year in Washington, Democrats need control of the Senate. Without it, much — maybe even most — of an agenda by a President Joe Biden will be dead on arrival in a Republican-controlled Senate.
left.roundup: People across the country will vote in 35 U.S. Senate elections Tuesday, with some being more contested than others. Republicans currently enjoy a 53-47 majority in the Senate, but Democrats now have a chance to establish their own majority. The presidential election is also an important factor here; in the event of a 50-50 tie vote in the Senate, the vice president casts the tie-breaking vote. center.title: Control of the Senate hangs in the balance on Election Day. Here are key Senate races to watch
center.body: The presidential election isn't the only critical race happening on November 3. Democrats and Republicans will battle across the country over control of the Senate. The Senate is currently split 53-47 between Republicans and Democrats. There are 35 seats up for election in the Senate, and of those, 23 belong to Republicans and 12 to Democrats. Democrats would need to win four seats for a majority, or three seats if Democrats win the White House. There are now nine Republican-held seats rated as either leaning Democratic or toss-ups

right.title: US Senate and congressional races to watch on Election Day 2020
right.body: A number of hotly contested congressional races could rival the drama and fascination of the main contest between President Trump and Democratic challenger Joe Biden on Election Day and possibly beyond. Republicans control the upper chamber by a 53-47 majority but that could be in jeopardy in Tuesday’s presidential election as some GOP senators are locked in highly competitive contests, including Sens. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina and Susan Collins of Maine. Democrats would need to pick up four seats to snatch majority control or three seats if Joe Biden
